new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (34 pp., the PDF's metadata gives the title 'Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea', authors Claassen & McElhanon) opened. Both quoted passages are there verbatim at the stated locators: extracted text page 10 = printed p. 54, sec. 2.4.5 'One other language has been reported to be spoken at the villages of Bonkiman and Wandabong (pop. c.500). No word list was obtained but informants stated that the language is similar to the Kewieng language and so it is provisionally included in the Yupna family.' (page image confirms 'c.500'; the scanned text renders it '0.500'); extracted text page 22 = printed p. 66, syllable-structure paragraph of sec. 6.1: 'Stress is phonemic in Rawa but…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for Bonkiman is stated anywhere. The only remark is a family-level one: in the 'Yupna' language (the authors' Kewieng = Yopno data) stress is 'probably sub-phonemic', i.e. non-contrastive and predictable, with a light functional load; the position of stress is not given. Bonkiman itself was never sampled (no word list obtained), so this applies to Bonkiman only by the survey's provisional grouping.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Yupna/Bonkiman. Footnote 11 (p. 78) concerns Wantoat only: Davis (1961) found stress differences in near-identical environments, but Davis (1967) states stress is non-phonemic.
new_statements.domain_note: NOT a first-hand description of Bonkiman: the sentence is about 'Yupna' (the Kewieng language of the upper Yupna valley, = Yopno yopn1238) and the Finisterre stock in general; word-level (syllable/phoneme discussion), based on 1968-69 survey word lists. Bonkiman was reported second-hand by informants and provisionally placed in the Yupna family without data.
new_statements.identity_note: Claassen & McElhanon 1970: 54 locate the language at the villages of Bonkiman and Wandabong (pop. c. 500) and never obtained a word list; Smith 1988: 95 says Bonkiman 'is only spoken in the village of Yuwong on the north coast of the Huon Peninsula' — the two sources disagree on location. The 'Yupna' of the p. 66 stress remark is the Kewieng language of the upper Yupna valley = Yopno (yopn1238, ISO yut), not Bonkiman; Glottolog places Bonkiman under Kewieng-Bonkiman-Nokopo (kewi1241) within Yupna (yupn1242).
